dial.summary: DXY broke below 100 to 99.09 following the BOJ's September 18 +25bps hike, neutralising the dollar headwind and leaving real yields at 2.66% as the sole structural obstacle; TOTAL pulled back ~$120B to $2.75T after Friday's 5.85% surge but BTC.D held above 56% and near-zero funding at 0.008% confirms continued spot-driven accumulation rather than leveraged speculation, sustaining BTC Accumulation conditions ahead of the data-dense week of September 30 (PCE, GDP) and October 2 (NFP).

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $103,511B (~$103.5T) as of September 2026 per MacroMicro/StreetStats (6–8 week lag; July is the last fully reported month); US M2 alone reached $23.2T in July 2026; 4-week trend up confirmed (sustained expansion from ~$103.0T in late August to $103.5T in mid-September); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); BOJ's September 18 hike (+25bps to 1.25%) will modestly affect yen-denominated G4 components going forward but has no near-term impact on the reported aggregate.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down (Jul 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp); September ISM not released until October 1; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); S&P Global Flash PMI September 23 is the next advance read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY eased to ~99.09 on September 20, 2026 (weekend FX, per Trading Economics) following the BOJ's +25bps hike to 1.25% on September 18 which drove a strong yen rally; last official NY close was 100.2093 on September 18 (Friday); 4-week trend down: ~99.60 (Aug 18) → 99.09 (Sep 20) = −0.51 points (−0.51%, just above the 0.5% flat threshold); status neutral — DXY broke below the 100 threshold into the 97.5–100 neutral band, shifting from headwind for the first time since late August; the prior session's FOMC-driven USD rally has been fully unwound by the BOJ carry-trade reversal.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) closed at 2.66% on September 18, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.15 (next release September 21 will cover week through Sep 19); up from 2.653% at the September 17 TIPS reopening auction (18-year high per TipsWatch); 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 19) → 2.66% (Sep 18) = +21bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); real yields remain the primary macro drag on duration-sensitive and risk assets; DXY neutralising below 100 is a partial offset but real yields at 2.66% keep the headwind count at one; sustainably falling below 2% required to shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 18, 2026 close: 10Y ~4.94%, 2Y ~4.74% (per MacroRadar/centralbank.watch); spread = +0.20% (+20bps); 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+38bps (Aug 18, pre-FOMC) → +20bps (Sep 18) = −18bps, driven by front-end repricing as 2Y anchors to fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); curve flattening continued as the 10Y rallied on BOJ yen strength, compressing the spread; the October 27–28 FOMC will be the next key repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747B ($6.747T) for week ending September 16, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 17 (Treasuries $4,554B, MBS $1,914B, other $279B); next H.4.1 release scheduled September 24, 2026; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.747T (Sep 16) = +$47B, marginal expansion within the flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilisation plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity, not new asset purchases); total assets up $138B year-on-year (from $6,609B).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.008% per 8h (range 0.0073%–0.0085% per 8h per MacroMicro/TheBlock as of September 18–19, 2026); Coinglass direct access unavailable due to network egress policy; near-zero funding during and after the September 19 TOTAL surge (+5.85% to $2.87T) and the subsequent $120B pullback to $2.75T on September 20 confirms the move was spot-driven, not a leveraged-long build-up; 30-day trend flat (funding has remained sub-0.01% throughout September as accumulation was orderly); status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold; near-zero is the ideal accumulation signal).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (September 20, 2026; CoinGecko data via search); total crypto market cap $2.75T (TOTAL pulled back $120B from $2.87T high on September 19 as profit-taking followed the 5.85% surge); stablecoin dominance 10.78% ($307B / $2.75T); one-day uptick from 10.67% (Sep 19) reflects TOTAL declining faster than stablecoin supply contracted, not new capital flowing into stablecoins; 30-day trend down: from ~11%+ (August 20) → 10.78% (Sep 20) = clear 30-day declining trend as capital deployed into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply); USDT $183.4B (60.57%), USDC $74.2B (24.1%); sustained sub-11% dominance alongside BTC.D above 56% is the primary BTC Accumulation signal this cycle.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: S&P Global US Flash PMI Composite, Manufacturing, and Services preliminary data for September 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first advance September activity read capturing the full post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) tightening cluster; DXY has since fallen to 99.09 as the yen rallied post-hike, partially easing the USD headwind; leads ISM Manufacturing (Oct 1) and ISM Services; a sub-50 manufacturing reading would materially shift November FOMC rate-path narrative; consensus expects modest softening from prior reads.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 20, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 20, 2026 — labor market read in the first full week post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ tightening cluster; a sustained rise above 220K would signal early labor market cracks under fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; prior weeks approximately 206K; labor resilience is key to the FOMC's case for sustained restrictive policy heading into October 27–28.

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Durable Goods Orders for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — watch non-defense capital goods ex-aircraft (key business investment proxy for Q3 GDP); elevated borrowing costs (10Y ~4.94%, real yields 2.66%) and DXY normalising near 99 weigh on capex decisions; ISM Manufacturing new orders fell to 53.7 in August (−3.0pp); Q2 2026 GDP third estimate follows September 30.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Final)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers final September 2026 reading at 10:00 AM ET — first final sentiment read fully incorporating the post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) trifecta; year-ahead inflation expectations closely watched; a sharp drop in current conditions or spike in inflation expectations could shift November FOMC positioning; released same day as Advance Durable Goods.
